title: Brief and pillars
summary: The original request, the premise, the six pillars and the art direction.
bodyHtml:
The request

A modernized horror take on Oregon Trail: a party you manage, members who fight and disagree, combat scenarios, an apocalyptic alternate world where the sky is turning blood red (the reason you are migrating), and supplies bought at the start. The core pillar: resources are always tight; there are constant hazards and people trying to trick you, but also people who genuinely need help; and you cannot stop for anything, because you must keep making forward progress or be consumed by the Great Haze.

Full text: docs/game-brief.md.

Premise

Nine winters ago the eastern sky stopped going dark and turned the color of a healing wound. The Great Haze, a bank of warm crimson fog a mile deep, rolls west across the country. What it takes does not die; it empties. The emptied are the Hollowed. The Meridian Company that once ran the Road has failed, and rumor places a blue sky, a wall and a gate past the mountains: the Blue Reach.

You are the wagon-master of a train leaving Cinder Ford, the last town the Haze has not reached. The Blue Reach is 840 miles away. The Haze starts 58 miles behind you and is faster than you are.

Pillars and how the rules enforce them

  • Resources are always tight: 600 scrip cannot fill the wagons; cargo has a hard cap; food, torches, physic and shot each drain on their own clock.
  • You can never stop for free: every option shows an hour cost, hours come out of that day's travel, and a halt day hands the Haze a full day.
  • The world is hostile: hazards, traps and raiders are constant; cargo, nerve and bodies can all be taken.
  • Some people genuinely need help: about half of strangers are genuine; helping is the only source of recruits, big finds and shortcuts, and refusing wears on the party.
  • Some people use your kindness: the other half are traps, in the same scene with the same words. Only the tells differ.
  • Progress or be consumed: the Haze is a gap in miles that shrinks unless you outrun it. Gap at or below 0 ends the run.

test/runs.test.ts measures these across seeded runs: careful discernment beats both reflexive kindness and reflexive suspicion, food runs dry in many but not all runs, never-stopping abandons real people, always-helping gets tricked.

Art direction

  • Frontier wagon train: canvas wagons, oxen, pitch torches. Torches are the signature image and the most important nightly cost.
  • Two sky moods. Far from the Haze: navy and teal, starfield, red stains bleeding into the sky. Close to the Haze: black smoke on oxblood cloud, a blood moon, ash-gray earth, blood in the ruts.
  • Blue is safety, red is the Haze, firelight is the only other warm color.
  • The sky is the gauge: four sky states keyed to distance (far, near, close, upon).

Details: docs/design.md (Art direction). The concept images are not committed to the repo.
